notes: Early ChatGPT (Nov 2022) predates gpt-3.5-turbo (Mar 2023) and is generally understood to be a text-davinci-00x-class 175B model rather than the later distilled turbo line. The dataset's note already says 175B is 'a GPT-3-scale proxy, not a disclosed GPT-3.5 size'. If the November 2022 backend was in fact an early turbo-class model, the 12B figure proposed for gpt-3.5-turbo would apply instead, which is why the low bound is wide. No central change.

Three-way conflict. (1) The softmax-bottleneck measurement (arXiv 2403.09539) recovers d_model = 4096 for gpt-3.5-turbo - a real measurement, not a guess - and the authors infer 'around 7 billion' parameters because 'most known transformer-based LLMs with embedding size 4,096 have approximately 7 billion parameters'. They flag the exception themselves: MoE architectures 'tend to have many more parameters per embedding dimension'. (2) Microsoft's CODEFUSION Table 1 listed 20B; Epoch carries that at 'Likely' confidence, while ALSO recording on its davinci-002 row that the paper 'was reportedly retracted because the authors did not know the parameter count'. That is an internal inconsistency in Epoch's own database. (3) IKP reads 246B TOTAL. All three reconcile under one architecture: an MoE with d_model = 4096, roughly 10-25B active and a couple of hundred B total. The 7B figure is only correct under a dense assumption the measurement does not establish. Raising the central to 12B, the geometric midpoint of 7B and 20B. UP 1.7x - flagged. Applies to the 0125, 1106 and Instruct records alike; the Instruct record already retains 20B and 175B as scenarios.

Epoch's database note for both GPT-4 Turbo snapshots reads 'Not known. Maybe smaller/sparser than GPT-4.' Serving evidence agrees in direction: GPT-4 Turbo listed at $10/$30 per Mtok against GPT-4 original's $30/$60, i.e. output price halved eight months later, and Epoch's own frontier-size article uses GPT-4 Turbo's 55 tok/s as the stepping stone between GPT-4 and GPT-4o. The dataset currently transfers GPT-4's 275B unchanged. 175B is the midpoint of a Turbo that is materially but not dramatically smaller; the geometric midpoint between GPT-4's 280B and GPT-4o's 50B would be 118B, which I judge too aggressive on this evidence. LOW CONFIDENCE JUDGMENT CALL: keeping 275B for family coherence is defensible, and the IKP factual-capacity reading actually ranks gpt-4-turbo (1.05T) above gpt-4 (622B), though that instrument is unreliable across eras.

Three routes. (1) Lambert: 5-7T total, ~600B active, from '5X parameters + 2X dataset size = 10X compute' relative to GPT-4; his own caveat is 'big error bars'. (2) Epoch's training compute: 3.8e26 FLOP at 'Likely' confidence, from 187M H100-hours at 20-40% utilisation. Inverting C = 6ND at GPT-4's overtraining ratio (D/N = 46) gives 1.2T active; at a more overtrained D/N = 100 it gives 800B; at D/N = 30 it gives 1.4T. (3) Price: $75/$150 per Mtok, 15x GPT-4o's output price nine months later, the highest OpenAI has ever charged, and API access was withdrawn 2025-07-14 rather than repriced - consistent with a model too expensive to serve. All three point at or above Lambert's 600B, so I move the central up to 800B. This is a 1.33x change, below the reporting threshold, but the direction is worth knowing.

IKP puts GPT-4.1 at 2.2T total, the largest pre-GPT-5.5 OpenAI entry, well above GPT-4o's 392B. But GPT-4.1 is priced BELOW GPT-4o ($2/$8 against $2.50/$10) at comparable speed, which bounds active parameters at or below GPT-4o's. The two reconcile if GPT-4.1 is a sparser, more knowledge-dense model: larger total, similar or smaller active. Since the dataset needs active parameters, the serving evidence governs. No change.

Existing prior came from a reported accuracy comparison with Mistral Small 24B, which establishes nothing about architecture. It now has genuine independent support: IKP reads 501B total, which at ~20x 2025-era sparsity gives ~25B active. Priced $0.40/$1.60, between GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1. Rounded to 25B from 24B - a 1.04x change, i.e. effectively no change, but the confidence basis is much better than 'weak size prior'.

Priced $0.10/$0.40 per Mtok at 117 tok/s. IKP reads 71B total; at ~10x sparsity that is ~7B active. The existing Ministral-8B-comparator prior survives contact with the independent evidence. No change.

Two signals point above the GPT-4o-transferred 50B: o1 launched at $15/$60 per Mtok, six times GPT-4o's output price, and IKP reads 1.3T total against GPT-4o's 392B. Both are weak. The price signal is undercut by OpenAI's own o3 announcement - an 80 percent cut with 'Same exact model-just cheaper' - which shows reasoning-model list prices carried roughly 5x margin over serving cost. MEDEC's o1-preview ~300B and o1-mini ~100B are the only figures in that paper not traceable to prior public estimates, but they carry the authors' blanket 'cannot vouch' disclaimer. Artificial Analysis publishes no throughput for o1, so the one route that would settle it is unavailable. Nudged to 60B; 1.2x, below the reporting threshold.
